money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Gambian Dalasi (GMD). Good options for currency exchange include: the Atlantic coast resorts the tourist area of Senegambia The Gambia is a cash-based economy. Credit cards aren't accepted by many hotels, restaurants or retail outlets. Major hotels generally accept them, but sometimes telecommunication issues can make payments difficult. There are a limited range of ATMs that accept foreign cards. Contact your bank to check if your cards will work in The Gambia. Make sure you have enough cash to meet your needs.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. The Gambian authorities will take strong action against anyone importing, exporting or found in possession of drugs. Don't accept packages on behalf of anyone without knowing their contents. They can include lengthy jail terms. Foreign nationals have been jailed for up to 10 years for carrying small amounts of cannabis.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: The death penalty can apply for: arson treason murder The Gambia resumed executions in 2012. In February 2018, President Barrow announced a moratorium on the death penalty. Corporal punishment applies for some crimes such as: assault sexual assault theft serious driving offences
laws.heading: Death penalty and corporal punishment

laws.rule: It's illegal to take photos of military facilities, or to take photos in and around airports. Some prescription or over-the-counter drugs are illegal. Penalties can be severe, including heavy fines or jail terms. See Health.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships are illegal. Penalties include jail terms from five years to life. There has been an increase in discrimination, including by government officials.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ information

laws.rule: The Gambia is a mostly Islamic country. Standards of dress and behaviour, especially in interior areas of the country, are conservative. Wear loose clothes that cover your shoulders and knees. Take care not to offend.
laws.heading: Information on dress

laws.rule: The Islamic holy month of Ramadan is observed. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. During Ramadan, eating, drinking and smoking may be illegal in public during the day. If you're not fasting, avoid these activities around people who are. Seek local advice to avoid offence. Explore our Ramadan page to learn more, including dates for Ramadan.
laws.heading: Ramadan

laws.rule: It's illegal to import, use or possess medication containing: codeine diazepam hydroquinone hydrocortisone betamethasone flucinonide clobestatol clobestatone Other restrictions may apply. Check with the High Commission of The Gambia before you travel. Pharmacy regulation is limited, and counterfeit medications are a risk. Bring all essential, legal medication with you.
laws.heading: Medication

laws.rule: To drive you'll need both: a valid Australian driver's licence an International Driving Permit (IDP) You must get your IDP before you leave Australia.
laws.heading: Driving permit

visa-preparation.entry_summary: Smartraveller says an Australian may need a visa for The Gambia; contact the High Commission of The Gambia. A compulsory Security Airport Fee of US$20 is paid on entering and leaving by air, and a yellow fever certificate is needed.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Not settled on the pages read: ask the High Commission of The Gambia in writing whether a visa is needed.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Confirm the visa position with the High Commission, carry a yellow fever certificate, and plan to pay the Security Airport Fee at the Banjul airport kiosks.

steps.step: Ask the High Commission of The Gambia whether a visa is needed for the purpose and length of stay.
Pay the Security Airport Fee at the marked kiosks at Banjul International Airport on arrival and on departure (children under 2 and transit passengers exempt).
Carry a yellow fever vaccination certificate.
Driving in from Senegal: a vehicle registration fee may be asked at the border.

documents: Visa if the High Commission says one is needed
Cash or card for the airport security fee

fees.item: Security Airport Fee, each way by air (or equivalent in EUR, GBP or dalasi)

open_questions: Do Australians need a visa in advance, on arrival, or neither? The atlas said visa-free up to 90 days; Smartraveller says 'may need a visa'.

Gambia Tourism Board do's and don'ts: dress modestly and don't show your thighs in public, including at religious and sacred sites. Men shouldn't go bare-chested away from the beach.
